text: So how do sodium ions cross this barrier? Through transport proteins: this is their transport role. Watch a sodium ion reach the bilayer: the core turns it back. Now it meets a channel protein, one of the proteins that span the bilayer. Down its middle runs a pore, lined with hydrophilic parts of the protein and filled with water, so the ion passes through without touching the hydrophobic core. Each kind of channel lets particular ions or polar molecules through; different channels pass different ones. And notice that the channel keeps its shape the whole time.
